newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Arafat willing to meet Israel's Netanyahu - aide.
newsitem.headline: Arafat willing to meet Israel's Netanyahu - aide.

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat is willing to meet Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu provided the talks focus on ending a crisis over Israel's settlement policy, an Arafat aide said on Thursday.

"The president is willing to meet Netanyahu if the meeting is to discuss the latest Israeli measures, including the settlement in (Arab East Jerusalem) and (West Bank) redeployment," Marwan Kanafani told Reuters.
There was no immediate comment from Netanyahu's office.
Kanafani's statement came amid Israeli-Arab tensions heightened by the killing of seven Israeli schoolgirls by a Jordanian soldier on the Israel-Jordan border.

Israel said that senior Palestine Liberation Organisation official Mahmoud Abbas, also known as Abu Mazen, phoned Israeli Foreign Minister David Levy on Thursday to express condolences over the killing.

"He said that 'this an event of extreme gravity which touches the heart of all of us because innocent children were the victims'," Israeli Foreign Ministry spokesman Danny Shek quoted Abu Mazen as saying.
Israeli-PLO relations deteriorated after Netanyahu's government last month approved plans to build 6,500 more homes for Jews in Arab East Jerusalem.

Relations plunged further when the Israeli government announced last week that a West Bank pullback, one of three due to be completed by mid-1998, would be only a third of the size demanded by the PLO.

Abu Mazen, architect of the 1993 Israel-PLO self-rule deal and chief Palestinian negotiator with Israel, tendered his resignation to Arafat in protest at the Israeli moves. Arafat has yet to decide whether to accept the resignation.
